pharm: Synthetic fluorinated topical glucocorticoid with anti-inflammatory, antipruritic, and vasoconstrictive actions on the skin.
quick: Apply thin film to affected area 2-4 times daily
Use sparingly; smallest amount for shortest time
Avoid application to nipple/breast; use caution
Local skin effects; HPA axis if extensive/occluded use
summary: Fluocinolone acetonide is a synthetic topical corticosteroid for the relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses. It is applied as a thin film two to four times daily. Prolonged use, application over large areas, or occlusion increases systemic absorption and the risk of HPA-axis suppression and local skin effects such as atrophy.
indications: Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses (e.g., eczema/atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis)

dosage.t: 2 to 4 times daily depending on severity
dosage.n: Part hair in hairy sites for direct contact

dosage.t: As above, occlusive dressing may be used

dosage.n: Children more susceptible to systemic toxicity and HPA suppression

admin: Apply a thin film to the affected area and rub in gently
In hairy sites, part the hair to allow direct contact with the lesion
Use occlusive dressings only for psoriasis/recalcitrant conditions; discontinue if infection develops
Avoid application to the face, groin, and axillae unless directed
Wash hands after application; avoid contact with eyes
moa: Topical corticosteroids bind cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors and induce phospholipase A2-inhibitory proteins (lipocortins), reducing release of arachidonic acid and downstream inflammatory mediators (prostaglandins, leukotrienes); produces anti-inflammatory, antipruritic, immunosuppressive, and vasoconstrictive effects in skin.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to fluocinolone or any component of the preparation
relative: Untreated cutaneous bacterial, fungal, or viral infection at the site
Application to large body surface area or under occlusion
Use on thin skin (face, intertriginous areas)
monitor: Signs of HPA-axis suppression with extensive/prolonged use

preg: Use only if clearly needed; apply the smallest amount for the shortest time and avoid extensive use or occlusion during pregnancy.
lact: Systemically administered corticosteroids appear in milk; use caution. Do not apply to the breast/nipple area before nursing.
renal: No dosage adjustment needed (minimal systemic absorption with proper topical use).

interactions.diagnostics: Extensive/occluded use may suppress HPA axis - consider ACTH stimulation, AM cortisol, or urinary free cortisol if suppression suspected.

emergency: Adrenal crisis (with abrupt withdrawal after systemic suppression)

monitoring: Signs of systemic absorption/HPA suppression with large-area, occlusive, or prolonged use (especially in children)
Therapeutic response; reassess if no improvement
counsel: Apply a thin layer only to the affected skin as directed
Do not use on the face or skin folds, or under bandages, unless told to
Do not use for longer than prescribed
Avoid getting it in the eyes
Tell your clinician if the skin condition worsens or shows signs of infection
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect within hours to days
Local; depends on skin condition and occlusion
Variable (minimal systemic absorption with normal use)
Store at room temperature; avoid freezing
pearls: Potency and systemic absorption rise with occlusion, broken skin, large surface area, and thin skin
Children have higher skin surface-to-weight ratio and greater risk of systemic effects/HPA suppression
Available in multiple vehicles (cream, ointment, solution, oil, shampoo) of differing potency
Avoid abrupt withdrawal after prolonged high-potency use; taper if HPA suppression possible
Treat underlying infection - corticosteroids can mask or worsen cutaneous infections
missed: If a dose is missed, apply it when remembered. If it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed dose. Do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Topically applied corticosteroids can be absorbed in sufficient amounts to produce systemic effects (HPA suppression, hyperglycemia, glucosuria) with excessive or prolonged use. Discontinue or reduce frequency; manage systemic effects supportively.
